items.explanation: Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but both prescriptions were written that day and both remain current on 9/24/2026: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (7/15/2026-12/26/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (7/15/2026-12/25/2026). The rivaroxaban order was never discontinued, so the patient is on duplicate anticoagulation with a high bleeding risk. Confirm which agent is intended and cancel the other.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list medication) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 3/2/2026 - the outpatient order was authored that day and citalopram appears on the medication list for the first time in that note. Because the start was after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies: obtain an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met. (The 3/7/2026 citalopram order is a refill at the same dose and does not create a new requirement.)

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily (QT watch-list medication) was started on this chart at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026, when the first outpatient order was authored. Under the revised memo effective 3/1/2026 an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded on 4/29/2026 - 19 days after the start - so it falls outside the required 14-day window and no qualifying ECG was obtained. The requirement was due before the 9/24/2026 evaluation date and remains unmet (it would only have counted under the superseded 30-day memo).

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily (QT watch-list medication) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026 - the outpatient order was authored that day and escitalopram appears on the medication list for the first time in that note (absent on 6/24/2026). Under the revised memo effective 3/1/2026 an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 12/25/2025, before the start, so no ECG has been obtained since escitalopram was started. The requirement is past due as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily (QT watch-list medication) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026; escitalopram appears on the medication list for the first time in that note. Under the revised memo effective 3/1/2026 an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. An ECG on 8/18/2026 would fall within the required window, so whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list medication) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026 - the outpatient order was authored that day and haloperidol appears on the medication list for the first time in that note. Under the revised memo effective 3/1/2026 an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been recorded since the start (her last ECG is 104253928 from 3/9/2025), but the deadline is after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date, so the follow-up ECG is not yet due.

At the cardiology clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a warfarin dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR(PT) was drawn on 9/5/2026 and was 2.3, four days after the change, so the monitoring requirement was met.

The anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 9/10/2026 documents a home INR of 3.4 and decreases warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, which the 3/1/2026 standing order permits and the 3/1/2026 memo covers. An INR was therefore required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 8/22/2026; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the follow-up INR is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

71-year-old man (DOB 8/23/1955) with documented atrial fibrillation carried on the active problem list and repeated in every cardiology clinic note through 7/28/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1), for which the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline gives a Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation. No anticoagulant is current as of 9/24/2026; the only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily and no anticoagulant has ever been prescribed in this chart. Note prior hemorrhage complicating a procedure, so bleeding risk should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs clinical review.

71-year-old woman (DOB 9/7/1955) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I48.0) on the problem list. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (prior cerebral infarction/stroke 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female sex 1), well above the threshold at which the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation (Class 1). No anticoagulant is current as of 9/24/2026 - current medications are rate-control and symptomatic therapy only (metoprolol/carvedilol, famotidine). Paroxysmal AF does not lower stroke risk, and the most recent ECG (3/14/2025) being in sinus rhythm does not remove the indication. Start/document a decision on anticoagulation.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-prescribed on 8/20/2026 (current through 12/28/2026) despite outside records reviewed on 8/12/2026 documenting an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with hemoglobin nadir 6.9 and 2 units transfused, after which apixaban was explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The 8/20/2026 clinic note simply says continue current regimen and lists apixaban plus aspirin and clopidogrel, so triple antithrombotic therapy has been resumed after a major bleed without the documented cardiology decision. Anticoagulation for the atrial flutter should not continue without that review.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: ECG 107914094 (6/10/2026 17:13) and ECG 103088543 (6/10/2026 19:36) both show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at about 134 and 136 bpm respectively (RR coefficient of variation 0.18 and 0.16), i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate - consistent with her documented unspecified atrial fibrillation. The rhythm and rate documented in the note are wrong and the discrepancy needs reconciliation.

79-year-old man on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug, current order 7/29/2026-1/5/2027) for atrial fibrillation. His most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025) is sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT: QT about 500-525 ms with RR 968 ms gives a Bazett QTc of about 520 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT-monitoring memo of 1/15/2025, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes (4/20/2026) are not contributory: potassium 4.4 mEq/L, magnesium 2.2 mg/dL. He is also on warfarin; no repeat ECG has been obtained since 11/24/2025.

Most recent electrolytes (2/14/2026): potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (low-normal). No ECG has been repeated in over four years while amiodarone has been continued.
